title: Light-theme swipe cart icons have low contrast over translucent Green feedback
scope: User selected UI-028 on 2026-11-06 and accepted the fix on 2026-11-07. Improve local cart/bin/arrow readability while preserving action hues, translucency, gestures, animation, layout and model behavior.
environment: Qt 6.12.0 MSVC 2022 x64; offscreen/software and native Windows D3D11 WARP. Native Android x86_64 on isolated QShopper_API_36 emulator-5580 with disposable SQLite/settings. ARM64 phone APK built; no physical-device installation by agent.
evidence: Across Light-theme samples, check cart-body contrast falls to 2.274:1 and uncheck to 2.269:1. Per-state medians include 2.806:1 and 2.697:1, below the 3:1 meaningful-icon review target. Foreground is #fffbfe on the rendered 0.8-opacity Material Green500 strip.

Dark sampled cart bodies remain above 4.35:1. Light delete has a narrow 2.993:1 minimum but substantially higher medians; include its foreground/arrow combination rather than asserting all deletion frames are unclear.

The original values are measured at actual opaque body cores against the same pixels with the icon hidden. Antialiased edges are not the nominal foreground. See reviews/UX-002/measurements.json and normal frames.

Bin/cart silhouettes provide the non-color distinction when red/green become similar. Faint bodies therefore weaken that cue. The offline model preview is not Android correction output or a recognition study.
source_notes: TextDelegate uses fixed Red500/Green500 at 0.8 opacity, separate from user primary/accent shades. TextIcon bodies inherit Material.backgroundColor; CartOut/Trash explicitly use the normal Theme context.
ArrowIcon uses Material.primaryTextColor for its arrow. A body-only switch to dark ink could make the Light arrow disappear into it; evaluate both together.
The new review probe's separate RHI assertion has no established cause and is not treated as this contrast bug or a confirmed opacity-binding defect.
reproduction: Run the explicit UX-002 review probe under its documented native Windows software renderer and inspect Light check/uncheck frames over the bakery/evening-produce backgrounds.
Before implementing, reproduce on the actual app with a held deliberate swipe, in both directions and in shopping/edit modes, including checked and unchecked rows.

Capture real Android rendering with isolated data and inspect sufficient feedback reveal and relevant animation phases. System color-space simulator screenshots alone cannot prove the displayed simulation.
expected: Meaningful cart/bin/arrow shapes remain discernible against the actual composed feedback surface, with a 3:1 review target and rounding margin where applicable. Preserve action semantics, existing non-color cues, vivid theme choices and one-handed gestures.
acceptance_criteria: Add a permanent real-trigger regression first and confirm failure with the original Light cart pairing, then pass with the selected fix. Distinguish application behavior from review-fixture failures.
Evaluate body and arrow together against actual backgrounds in Light/Dark/System, both directions and edit/shopping/checked states, including live theme changes and representative image extremes.
Retain red deletion and green shopping semantics unless separately agreed, and avoid changing global primary/accent tones to fix this local feedback role.
Validate the actual Android swipe paths, saved check/delete outcomes and non-color recognition cues. Record platform/simulation limits and physical-phone acceptance before closure.

implementation.summary: ArrowIcon.qml uses black cart/bin bodies in both themes and white directional arrows with black Text.Outline. Removed its unused Material import. The shared base covers CartInIcon, CartOutIcon and TrashIcon; global TextIcon colors are unchanged.
implementation.preserved: Material Red500 deletion and Green500 checking/unchecking at 0.8 opacity, the existing animated arrows and opacity, geometry, sensitivity, half-width/velocity triggers, pullback, ordering, saved data and Undo policy.

regression.windows_test: tests/swipecontrast/tst_swipecontrast.qml::test_held_swipe, registered in normal qshopper_swipecontrast_tests and qshopper_swipecontrast_rendering_tests. Production ShopView, actual touch press/move/hold/release, all directions/modes/check states/themes, white/black/two photos, body and arrow pixels, live theme/palette changes, actual check/delete and Undo outcomes. 66 offscreen and 68 native records including setup/cleanup.
regression.windows_before: out/ui028/before.txt: original Light/shop/unchecked/right/white body contrast 2.177:1 fails 3:1 after a real held touch crosses half width. Two setup/cleanup records pass.
regression.windows_after: All 15 Windows CTest entries pass, totaling 1063 records with zero failures/skips. Eight general suites and seven new/existing contrast/native suites were covered in disjoint filtered runs. Logs: out/ui028/general-windows-tests.log, native-windows-tests.log, swipe-tests-final.log and swipe-rhi-final.log. New native entry was rechecked with D3D11 WARP: 68 records, 142.52 seconds. An initial exact-black outline-edge assertion caused seven fixture failures per new suite; measuring actual antialiased darkened outline pixels corrects that assertion. No production change was needed for those failures.
regression.android_test: tests/android/test_swipecontrast.py: actual held/cancelled native swipe, same-frame opaque body cores against adjacent tinted pixels, arrow visibility, then separate committed swipe and exact saved UUID/name/check outcomes. 20 Light/Dark/System profiles. Screenshots do not establish native color-vision simulation.
regression.android_before: out/ui028/android-before/results.json: original Light cart body 2.438:1 fails 3:1 with a valid paired capture. Applying the final same-frame adjacent-pixel algorithm to that original held screenshot also fails at 2.346:1; see reprocessed.json.
regression.android_driver_notes: Earlier paired-frame attempts were invalidated by slideshow changes; the final driver compares opaque body cores with adjacent tinted pixels from one frame. Earlier wall-clock captures sampled partial fades, the deliberately outgoing CartOut arrow, or the timed return; those invalid runs remain under out/ui028. BackGesture.java now acknowledges HELD after actual movement and waits for a stdin acknowledgement after both captures; existing timed gesture paths are unchanged. The driver retries only fresh UI-tree dumps, matching existing native scripts. An earlier run was interrupted by emulator host-GPU external-memory/context errors and ADB timeout; the task-owned emulator was restarted before the final synchronized run. These driver/host failures are not additional application defects.
regression.android_after: Final synchronized native matrix passes all 100 checks across 20 profiles, with zero failures: out/ui028/android-final-synced/results.json and out/ui028/android-final-synced.log. Actual opaque black body cores versus adjacent same-frame feedback measure 3.929:1 to 5.043:1, above the 3:1 target. Early arrow visibility, preserved data after cancellation and exact committed check/delete results all pass. The final command exits 0 and restores the original OS night mode. Production frames were visually inspected; user accepted the fix on 2026-11-07.

resolution.acceptance: 2026-11-07: user stated: fix accepted, commit and close.
resolution.summary: Use black cart/bin bodies and white, black-outlined directional arrows on the existing red/green swipe strips in both themes. Preserve all gesture and model behavior.
resolution.regression: Permanent real-touch Windows and native Android tests, failing-before/passing-after evidence and capture-driver limitations are recorded above.
resolution.verification: All 15 Windows suites pass (1063 records), all 100 native Android checks pass, both APK package contracts pass, and all 65 tracked QML/templates pass formatter Check. User acceptance complements automated coverage.
resolution.remaining: None within the accepted UI-028 scope. UX-003 remains deferred; color-vision recognition and live system correction were not certified by RGB screenshots.
